units.t: Statistics: Tally Charts and Frequency Tables

unit.title: Numbers to 1000
unit.blurb: Reading, writing and making 3-digit numbers, comparing and ordering them, and rounding to the nearest 10 and 100.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Understand the value of each digit in a 3-digit number: hundreds, tens and ones.

O2.t: Compare and order numbers up to 1000 using the symbols <, > and =.

O3.t: Estimate and round 3-digit numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

p: A 3-digit number has **hundreds**, **tens** and **ones**. In **472** there are 4 hundreds, 7 tens and 2 ones.
In 405 there are no tens. The 0 keeps the 5 in the ones place.

p: To compare, look at the **hundreds** first. If they are the same, look at the **tens**, then the **ones**.
**<** means 'is less than' and **>** means 'is greater than': 345 < 354.

lesson.t: The mouth eats the bigger number
p: The open side of < or > always faces the bigger number.

p: To round to the nearest **10**, look at the **ones** digit. 5 or more rounds up; less than 5 rounds down. 347 → **350**.
To round to the nearest **100**, look at the **tens** digit. 347 → **300**.
45 is exactly halfway between 40 and 50. We round it up to 50.
